exposure: transfusion of ≥6 RBC units before the first cryoprecipitate
Time to first cryoprecipitate transfusion (<6 RBC units vs ≥6 RBC units)
cohort: 249 women with MOH (defined as bleeding at ≥20 weeks' gestation or postpartum requiring ≥5 red blood cells units within 4 h) identified from the Australian and New Zealand Massive Transfusion Registry between 2008 and 2015
finding: Transfusion of ≥6 red blood cell units before the first cryoprecipitate, placenta praevia, and emergency caesarean section were independently associated with an increased risk of hysterectomy in women with MOH.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section was independently associated with an increased risk of hysterectomy in cases of massive obstetric haemorrhage.
